_comment: Per-item judgement by the meeting's own participant on the extracted task list. This is the only ground truth of its kind we have: someone who was in the room saying which items are real. Nine LLM runs across three admission rules were scored against it (spec section 12).

true_tasks.label: Outlook calendar integration
true_tasks.note: Judged a real action. Not caught by any rule in 9 runs except once -- it reads as product scope rather than an assignment.

true_tasks.label: AI knowledge base for construction terms
true_tasks.note: Judged a real action. Same shape as A and missed for the same reason.

true_tasks.label: Downtown proposal review, Friday 2 PM
true_tasks.note: The least ambiguous item in the meeting -- explicit time, explicit invitation, explicit yes. A rule that drops this is too strict.

true_tasks.label: Two devices to Clement to test the new system
true_tasks.note: The existing extractor missed this one entirely; every brief run caught it.

not_tasks.label: Restrict Josh's website access
not_tasks.note: Raised before and pushed back on in the room: 'I know, but you can't block him.' The refusal is IN the transcript -- a rule that reads the reply catches this.

not_tasks.label: Train Deon Jay in reality capture
not_tasks.note: The speaker describing their own arrangement. The other party said only 'mm'.

not_tasks.label: AWS credits / independent front end
not_tasks.note: Already applied for. The reply describes something already under way rather than taking anything on.

unresolved.label: Follow up on drone / right-of-way usage
unresolved.note: The participant did not remember it. Both the extractor and every brief run produced it, so it is more likely real and forgotten than invented. Left unscored.

measured.why: Precision and recall traded almost exactly across three rules aimed at different things, and the spread between rules was smaller than one rule's own run-to-run variance. Recall was chosen: a missed task is one the recorder still remembers; a surplus one is dismissed in the UI.

models._comment: 3 models x 3 rules x 3 runs on the same session. Scores are (real found of 5, false found of 3).
models.conclusion: 3.8-max loses to 3.7-max in every cell. flash matches max on score and is not faster (88-162s either way). The rule moves the result more than the model does; run-to-run variance moves it more than both.
